26logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

27 

28DEFAULT_LOWER = 0.125 

29DEFAULT_UPPER = 0.3333333333333333 

30 

31# One Philox call yields four values, so a program of the fused training kernel 

32# covers ``BLOCK * _UNROLL`` elements; the kernel calls its group helper once 

33# per value, and spells that 4 out because a kernel cannot read this module 

34# constant. This is the tiling the ``uniform`` kernel uses, and it has to stay 

35# that way: the counter of a value follows from its element index, so the same 

36# generator state drawn on a different tiling gives different numbers. 

37_UNROLL = 4 

38 

39# The fused training kernel addresses elements by a flat offset, which the 

40# generated kernel carries as an int32. 

41_INT32_MAX = torch.iinfo(torch.int32).max 

42 

43# Hash-RNG grid cap: GCU400 ships 24 SIPs and 48 CTAs (2 per SIP) is the 

44# measured concurrency sweet spot for streaming kernels (dropout/xlogy/ 

45# rrelu_with_noise_backward precedent). 

46_NUM_SLOTS = 48 

47 

48# 2^-24 / 2^-16: the fp32 sampling grid of one hash word, full and the 

49# 16-bit split used for reduced dtypes (uniform_ precedent). 

50_U24 = tl.constexpr(5.960464477539063e-8) 

51_U16 = tl.constexpr(1.52587890625e-5) 

52 

53# Non-contiguous in-place calls are computed on contiguous copies and written 

54# back through the native copy; ``copy_`` has no private-use kernel for this 

55# keyset yet, so redispatch it past the GCU backend. 

56_NATIVE_COPY_KEYSET = torch._C.DispatchKeySet( 

57 torch._C.DispatchKey.CompositeExplicitAutograd 

58) 

59 

60 

61def _copy_back(dst, src): 

62 torch.ops.aten.copy_.default.redispatch(_NATIVE_COPY_KEYSET, dst, src, False)

65@pointwise_dynamic( 

66 is_tensor=[True, True], 

67 num_outputs=2, 

68 promotion_methods=[(0, 1, "DEFAULT"), (0, 1, "DEFAULT")], 

69) 

70@triton.jit 

71def _rrelu_with_noise_train(self, noise): 

72 # ATen samples for self <= 0 (including signed zero), and records one for 

73 # positive/NaN elements. Keeping this predicate aligned with backward is 

74 # important because noise is the training-time gradient multiplier. 

75 not_positive = self <= 0 

76 effective_noise = tl.where(not_positive, noise, 1.0) 

77 output = tl.where(not_positive, self * effective_noise, self) 

78 return output, effective_noise

81@pointwise_dynamic( 

82 is_tensor=[True, False], 

83 num_outputs=1, 

84 promotion_methods=[(0, 1, "DEFAULT")], 

85) 

86@triton.jit 

87def _rrelu_with_noise_eval(self, slope): 

88 return tl.where(self > 0, self, self * slope)

91@libentry() 

92@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["slope", "N"]) 

93def _rrelu_with_noise_eval_kernel( 

94 x_ptr, 

95 out_ptr, 

96 N, 

97 slope, 

98 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

99 EVEN: tl.constexpr, 

100): 

101 """Eval over a contiguous tensor: the flat grid-stride streaming form. 

102 

103 The generic pointwise body measures ~0.7 TB/s on the core large shapes 

104 (11-12 bench log) while this backend's flat 1R/1W streaming kernels reach 

105 the ~2.9 TB/s DRAM floor (rrelu_with_noise_backward/xlogy precedent), so 

106 contiguous eval calls take the flat kernel; strided layouts keep the 

107 pointwise path. 

108 """ 

109 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

110 num_pids = tl.num_programs(0) 

111 lane = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

112 num_blocks = (N + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK 

113 for block_id in tl.range(pid, num_blocks, num_pids): 

114 off = block_id * BLOCK + lane 

115 if EVEN: 

116 x = tl.load(x_ptr + off) 

117 tl.store(out_ptr + off, tl.where(x > 0, x, x * slope)) 

118 else: 

119 mask = off < N 

120 x = tl.load(x_ptr + off, mask=mask, other=0.0) 

121 tl.store(out_ptr + off, tl.where(x > 0, x, x * slope), mask=mask) 

122 

123 

124@triton.jit 

125def _fmix32(x): 

126 # xxhash32-style avalanche finalizer: 8 cheap integer ops per uniform, 

127 # full avalanche (same hash family as this backend's dropout / randn / 

128 # uniform_ kernels). 

129 x = x ^ (x >> 15) 

130 x = tl.mul(x, 0x85EBCA77, sanitize_overflow=False) 

131 x = x ^ (x >> 13) 

132 x = tl.mul(x, 0xC2B2AE3D, sanitize_overflow=False) 

133 x = x ^ (x >> 16) 

134 return x 

135

137@triton.jit 

138def _rrelu_with_noise_train_group( 

139 x_ptr, noise_ptr, out_ptr, off, sampled, N, EVEN: tl.constexpr 

140): 

141 """Apply rrelu to one group of elements with its sampled slopes.""" 

142 # ATen samples for self <= 0 (including signed zero), and records one for 

143 # positive/NaN elements. Keeping this predicate aligned with backward is 

144 # important because noise is the training-time gradient multiplier. 

145 # ``out = x * effective_noise`` is written unconditionally: on the 

146 # positive arm it multiplies by the recorded unit slope, and 

147 # ``x * 1.0`` is bit-exact through the fp32 opmath round trip for every 

148 # input including NaN/Inf/signed zero. One vector multiply replaces a 

149 # multiply-plus-select per element. 

150 if EVEN: 

151 x = tl.load(x_ptr + off) 

152 effective_noise = tl.where(x <= 0, sampled, 1.0) 

153 tl.store(out_ptr + off, x * effective_noise) 

154 tl.store(noise_ptr + off, effective_noise) 

155 else: 

156 mask = off < N 

157 x = tl.load(x_ptr + off, mask=mask, other=0.0) 

158 effective_noise = tl.where(x <= 0, sampled, 1.0) 

159 tl.store(out_ptr + off, x * effective_noise, mask=mask) 

160 tl.store(noise_ptr + off, effective_noise, mask=mask) 

161 

162 

163@libentry() 

164@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["philox_seed", "philox_offset", "lower", "upper", "N"]) 

165def _rrelu_with_noise_train_kernel( 

166 x_ptr, 

167 noise_ptr, 

168 out_ptr, 

169 N, 

170 lower, 

171 upper, 

172 philox_seed, 

173 philox_offset, 

174 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

175 REDUCED: tl.constexpr, 

176 EVEN: tl.constexpr, 

177): 

178 """Training over a contiguous tensor, drawing the slopes in this kernel. 

179 

180 RNG note: the aten ``rrelu_with_noise`` accuracy contract in this suite is 

181 statistical (slope coverage of ``[lower, upper]``, per-generator-state 

182 reproducibility, stream advance) -- see tests/test_rrelu_with_noise.py. 

183 The philox4x32-10 chain costs ~15 dependent integer vector ops per element 

184 and dominated the wall of the previous philox version of this kernel 

185 (measured on uniform_: philox+conversion bucket 5.3 ms of a 6.07 ms total 

186 on 1 Gi fp16 vs a 0.72 ms store floor). This kernel therefore hashes the 

187 global element offset with the same xxhash32-style avalanche finalizer 

188 used by this backend's dropout / randn / uniform_ kernels. The per-call 

189 state is still drawn from / advances the torch philox generator via 

190 philox_backend_seed_offset (byte-identical increment accounting), so 

191 successive calls yield fresh independent samples and stay reproducible 

192 for a fixed generator state. The raw per-call state is avalanched into 

193 s0 first, otherwise two same-shape calls would return the same multiset 

194 of samples, merely permuted (dropout precedent, device-verified). 16-bit 

195 dtypes (REDUCED=True) split one 32-bit hash into a hi/lo pair of 16-bit 

196 uniforms, halving the hash budget; the fp32-domain slope arithmetic and 

197 the single rounding store match the aten opmath contract. 

198 """ 

199 rng_state = philox_offset.to(tl.int64) ^ philox_seed.to(tl.int64) 

200 s0 = _fmix32(rng_state.to(tl.uint32)) ^ _fmix32((rng_state >> 32).to(tl.uint32)) 

201 scale = upper - lower 

202 if REDUCED: 

203 s_u = scale * _U16 

204 else: 

205 s_u = scale * _U24 

206 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

207 num_pids = tl.num_programs(0) 

208 lane = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

209 num_blocks = (N + BLOCK * 4 - 1) // (BLOCK * 4) 

210 

211 for block_id in tl.range(pid, num_blocks, num_pids): 

212 off_0 = block_id * (BLOCK * 4) + lane 

213 off_1 = off_0 + BLOCK 

214 off_2 = off_1 + BLOCK 

215 off_3 = off_2 + BLOCK 

216 if REDUCED: 

217 # one hash feeds a pair of BLOCK lanes (groups 0/1 and 2/3) 

218 ha = _fmix32(off_0.to(tl.uint32) + s0) 

219 hb = _fmix32(off_2.to(tl.uint32) + s0) 

220 u0 = ha >> 16 

221 u1 = ha & 0xFFFF 

222 u2 = hb >> 16 

223 u3 = hb & 0xFFFF 

224 else: 

225 u0 = _fmix32(off_0.to(tl.uint32) + s0) >> 8 

226 u1 = _fmix32(off_1.to(tl.uint32) + s0) >> 8 

227 u2 = _fmix32(off_2.to(tl.uint32) + s0) >> 8 

228 u3 = _fmix32(off_3.to(tl.uint32) + s0) >> 8 

229 # slopes stay in fp32: RN(u * s_u + lower) with the grid scale 

230 # prefolded, matching the aten opmath (fp32 accumulate, one rounding 

231 # store into the output/noise dtype). 

232 r0 = tl.fma(u0.to(tl.float32), s_u, lower) 

233 r1 = tl.fma(u1.to(tl.float32), s_u, lower) 

234 r2 = tl.fma(u2.to(tl.float32), s_u, lower) 

235 r3 = tl.fma(u3.to(tl.float32), s_u, lower) 

236 _rrelu_with_noise_train_group(x_ptr, noise_ptr, out_ptr, off_0, r0, N, EVEN) 

237 _rrelu_with_noise_train_group(x_ptr, noise_ptr, out_ptr, off_1, r1, N, EVEN) 

238 _rrelu_with_noise_train_group(x_ptr, noise_ptr, out_ptr, off_2, r2, N, EVEN) 

239 _rrelu_with_noise_train_group(x_ptr, noise_ptr, out_ptr, off_3, r3, N, EVEN)

242def _check_rrelu_with_noise_args(self, noise, lower, upper): 

243 if self.shape != noise.shape: 

244 raise RuntimeError( 

245 "noise tensor must have the same shape as self. " 

246 f"Got self.shape = {tuple(self.shape)} " 

247 f"and noise.shape = {tuple(noise.shape)}" 

248 ) 

249 if self.device != noise.device: 

250 raise RuntimeError( 

251 f"self and noise must be on the same device, got " 

252 f"{self.device} and {noise.device}" 

253 ) 

254 if self.dtype != noise.dtype: 

255 raise RuntimeError( 

256 f"self and noise must have the same dtype, got " 

257 f"{self.dtype} and {noise.dtype}" 

258 ) 

259 if not self.is_floating_point(): 

260 raise RuntimeError( 

261 f"rrelu_with_noise is not implemented for dtype {self.dtype}" 

262 ) 

263 if not math.isfinite(float(lower)): 

264 raise RuntimeError(f"rrelu: lower bound must be finite, got {lower}") 

265 if not math.isfinite(float(upper)): 

266 raise RuntimeError(f"rrelu: upper bound must be finite, got {upper}") 

267 if float(lower) > float(upper): 

268 raise RuntimeError( 

269 f"Lower bound should be less than or equal to the upper bound, " 

270 f"got lower={lower} and upper={upper}" 

271 ) 

272 

273 

274def _fill_training_noise(noise, lower, upper, generator): 

275 # For a strided workspace, sample contiguously and let the training kernel 

276 # scatter effective noise into the caller's layout while producing output. 

277 if noise.is_contiguous(): 

278 noise.uniform_(float(lower), float(upper), generator=generator) 

279 return noise 

280 

281 sampled = torch.empty_like(noise, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format) 

282 sampled.uniform_(float(lower), float(upper), generator=generator) 

283 return sampled 

284 

285 

286def _new_output(self): 

287 # ``aten::rrelu_with_noise`` returns the out-of-place result in legacy 

288 # contiguous layout, whatever the input layout is, so the allocation cannot 

289 # keep ``empty_like``'s preserve_format default: a channels-last or strided 

290 # input would otherwise come back in its own layout. 

291 return torch.empty_like(self, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format) 

292 

293 

294def _choose_train_block_and_warps(n, itemsize): 

295 # BLOCK/num_warps bands (calibrated by probes on 2026-11-17, do_bench median w1000/r100, 

296 # full sweep of 11 configs × 3 dtypes × 3 bands, probe table in job tmp/probe_sweep2.log): 

297 # - tiny hits the launch floor: at n=4096, B2048/nw4 = 4.1-4.5us (from B4096, a 4x 

298 # overhang cliff at 15.4us+, larger tiles 47-183us); 

299 # - 16-bit single band B4096/nw2: best at both 16.7M/512Mi points (from B8192, the 16-bit cliff 

300 # is 5.3x, B65536 worst at 0.3x); nw2/nw4 differ by <0.3%; 

301 # - fp32 large band B32768/nw2 (best at both 16.7M 121.5us / 512Mi 3099.9us points), 

302 # B65536 exceeds the DSM limit (Required 1048576 > 917504, confirmed by probes). 

303 if n <= 2048: 

304 return 512, 4 

305 if n <= 4096: 

306 return 2048, 4 

307 if itemsize == 2: 

308 return 4096, 2 

309 if n <= (1 << 21): 

310 return 4096, 4 

311 return 32768, 2 

312 

313 

314def _choose_eval_block_and_warps(n, itemsize): 

315 # flat streaming bands (calibrated by probes the same day): eval is 1R/1W with no 4-unroll. 

316 # - 16-bit large band B65536/nw2: best at both mid 28.9-29.0us / big 689.9-697.9us points; 

317 # - fp32 large band B65536/nw2 hits the DRAM floor (512Mi 1398.1us = 2.93TB/s), 

318 # at the 16.7M band B32768/nw2 is slightly better (47.8us), so the cutoff is 2^24. 

319 if n <= 4096: 

320 return max(triton.next_power_of_2(n) // 2, 256), 2 

321 if n <= 65536: 

322 return 2048, 4 

323 if n <= (1 << 21): 

324 return 8192, 4 

325 if itemsize == 2: 

326 return 65536, 2 

327 if n <= (1 << 24): 

328 return 32768, 2 

329 return 65536, 2 

330

332def _launch_contiguous_eval(self, out, slope): 

333 n_elements = self.numel() 

334 block, num_warps = _choose_eval_block_and_warps(n_elements, self.element_size()) 

335 grid = (min(triton.cdiv(n_elements, block), _NUM_SLOTS),) 

336 even = n_elements % block == 0 

337 with torch_device_fn.device(self.device): 

338 # Retry on occasional P02 cold-compilation failures (same as _launch_contiguous_train). 

339 for attempt in range(3): 

340 try: 

341 _rrelu_with_noise_eval_kernel[grid]( 

342 self, 

343 out, 

344 n_elements, 

345 float(slope), 

346 BLOCK=block, 

347 EVEN=even, 

348 num_warps=num_warps, 

349 num_stages=1, 

350 ) 

351 return out 

352 except Exception: 

353 if attempt == 2: 

354 raise 

355 return out 

356 

357 

358def _launch_contiguous_train(self, noise, out, lower, upper, generator): 

359 """Run the training kernel that draws its own slopes. 

360 

361 The generator has to advance by as much as a ``uniform_`` over the same 

362 number of elements would move it, so the increment is the number of 

363 philox counters ``uniform_`` would consume, one per four elements. 

364 """ 

365 n_elements = self.numel() 

366 increment = triton.cdiv(n_elements, _UNROLL) 

367 philox_seed, philox_offset = philox_backend_seed_offset( 

368 increment, generator=generator 

369 ) 

370 block, num_warps = _choose_train_block_and_warps(n_elements, self.element_size()) 

371 grid = (min(triton.cdiv(n_elements, block * _UNROLL), _NUM_SLOTS),) 

372 even = n_elements % (block * _UNROLL) == 0 

373 with torch_device_fn.device(self.device): 

374 # P02: the external llvm converter occasionally fails on cold compilation (converterResult=-2 family), 

375 # retrying the launch to trigger recompilation recovers (precedent: xlogy/rrelu_with_noise_backward). 

376 for attempt in range(3): 

377 try: 

378 _rrelu_with_noise_train_kernel[grid]( 

379 self, 

380 noise, 

381 out, 

382 n_elements, 

383 float(lower), 

384 float(upper), 

385 philox_seed, 

386 philox_offset, 

387 BLOCK=block, 

388 REDUCED=self.element_size() == 2, 

389 EVEN=even, 

390 num_warps=num_warps, 

391 num_stages=1, 

392 ) 

393 return out 

394 except Exception: 

395 if attempt == 2: 

396 raise 

397 return out 

398

400def _rrelu_with_noise_impl( 

401 self, 

402 noise, 

403 lower=DEFAULT_LOWER, 

404 upper=DEFAULT_UPPER, 

405 training=False, 

406 generator=None, 

407 out=None, 

408): 

409 _check_rrelu_with_noise_args(self, noise, lower, upper) 

410 

411 if self.numel() == 0: 

412 return _new_output(self) if out is None else out 

413 

414 if training: 

415 # The fused kernel addresses elements by flat offset, so it covers 

416 # contiguous inputs whose element count fits an int32 index. Strided 

417 # inputs and larger tensors keep the workspace-filling path, which is 

418 # what makes the workspace necessary in the first place. 

419 if ( 

420 self.is_contiguous() 

421 and noise.is_contiguous() 

422 and self.numel() <= _INT32_MAX 

423 ): 

424 output = out if out is not None else _new_output(self) 

425 return _launch_contiguous_train( 

426 self, noise, output, lower, upper, generator 

427 ) 

428 sampled_noise = _fill_training_noise(noise, lower, upper, generator) 

429 output = out if out is not None else _new_output(self) 

430 _rrelu_with_noise_train(self, sampled_noise, out0=output, out1=noise) 

431 return output 

432 else: 

433 slope = (float(lower) + float(upper)) * 0.5 

434 output = out if out is not None else _new_output(self) 

435 # Contiguous inputs use the flat streaming kernel (1R/1W hits the DRAM floor); inputs with a layout 

436 # still take the pointwise path. 

437 if ( 

438 self.is_contiguous() 

439 and output.is_contiguous() 

440 and self.numel() <= _INT32_MAX 

441 ): 

442 return _launch_contiguous_eval(self, output, slope) 

443 _rrelu_with_noise_eval(self, slope, out0=output) 

444 return output 

445

447def rrelu_with_noise( 

448 self, 

449 noise, 

450 lower=DEFAULT_LOWER, 

451 upper=DEFAULT_UPPER, 

452 training=False, 

453 generator=None, 

454): 

455 """FlagGems implementation of aten.rrelu_with_noise. 

456 

457 Backward is not built here. This operator is registered on the device 

458 dispatch key, so ``aten::rrelu_with_noise`` keeps the autograd kernel PyTorch 

459 generates from its derivative formula, and that kernel calls the separately 

460 registered ``aten::rrelu_with_noise_backward`` op. Calling this Python API 

461 outside the dispatcher therefore returns a forward-only result. 

462 

463 The training kernel writes the effective noise back through a strided 

464 store, which mis-addresses the tail on this backend (measured with a 

465 channels-last workspace: the result was right, the noise buffer was not). 

466 Sample into a contiguous copy and write it back with the native copy. 

467 """ 

468 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME RRELU_WITH_NOISE") 

469 if training and not noise.is_contiguous(): 

470 noise_c = noise.contiguous() 

471 output = _rrelu_with_noise_impl( 

472 self, noise_c, lower, upper, training, generator 

473 ) 

474 _copy_back(noise, noise_c) 

475 return output 

476 return _rrelu_with_noise_impl(self, noise, lower, upper, training, generator) 

477 

478 

479def rrelu_with_noise_( 

480 self, 

481 noise, 

482 lower=DEFAULT_LOWER, 

483 upper=DEFAULT_UPPER, 

484 training=False, 

485 generator=None, 

486): 

487 """FlagGems implementation of aten.rrelu_with_noise_. 

488 

489 Backward is provided the same way as ``rrelu_with_noise``. 

490 

491 A strided ``self``/``noise`` cannot be the kernel's output on this backend: 

492 the pointwise store mis-addresses the tail when ``stride(-1) != 1`` 

493 (measured with a ``[:, ::2]`` view -- both tensors came back wrong). Run 

494 the implementation on contiguous copies and copy the results back. 

495 """ 

496 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME RRELU_WITH_NOISE_") 

497 if self.is_contiguous() and noise.is_contiguous(): 

498 return _rrelu_with_noise_impl( 

499 self, noise, lower, upper, training, generator, out=self 

500 ) 

501 

502 self_c = self.contiguous() 

503 noise_c = noise.contiguous() 

504 result = _rrelu_with_noise_impl( 

505 self_c, noise_c, lower, upper, training, generator, out=self_c 

506 ) 

507 _copy_back(self, result) 

508 if training: 

509 # Training consumes/updates the noise workspace; eval leaves it alone. 

510 _copy_back(noise, noise_c) 

511 return self
